title: SIS / ISIS screening for high dimensional models
text: screen="SIS" performs one marginal screen. screen="ISIS" repeats screening current model, incorporating predictions offsets, keeps best joint-fitting round. screen="auto" enables ISIS ultrahigh-dimensional designs. screen="none" fits supplied design directly. nsis controls SIS retained set ISIS batch. default ISIS batch GIC-based. small batch lets joint fitting remove false positives search progresses. Screening implemented Rcpp OpenMP supports ordinary GLMs, negative binomial, multinomial Cox models. fit$screening records selected predictors, screening rounds, elapsed time thread use. default screening uses physical cores, one thread fallback detection unavailable. code: set.seed(31) X <- matrix(rnorm(250*5000), 250, 5000) beta <- numeric(5000); beta[c(5, 50, 500)] <- c(2, -1.5, 1) y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(250) fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic",   screen="ISIS", screen.nthreads=2L, relaxed=TRUE) l0glmMetrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] #>   gic TP FP FN   TN F1_score MCC #> 1 797  3  0  0 4997        1   1

"aic": Akaike information criterion \(\lambda = 2\). prediction-oriented choice based estimated expected Kullback–Leibler loss (Akaike, 1974). often retains variables generally consistent exact support recovery. "bic": Bayesian information criterion \(\lambda = \log n\). conventional choice identifying parsimonious model candidate dimension fixed moderate (Schwarz, 1978). classical consistency guarantee requires correctly specified identifiable model regularity conditions; need control overfitting large model spaces. "gic": generalized information criterion \(\lambda = \log p\,\log\log n\). selection-oriented choice sparse problems, including high-dimensional settings. Fan Tang (2013), Corollary 1, justify choice assumptions design, response tails, signal strength candidate model path. consistent choice conditions, uniquely optimal penalty every finite sample. "ebic": linearized extended BIC \(\lambda = \log n + 2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\log p\), package default \(\gamma_{\rm EBIC}=\max\{0,1-\log n/(2\log p)\}\). accounts large model spaces (Chen Chen, 2008). implementation replaces combinatorial term \(2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\log {p \choose k}\) \(2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}k\log p\), giving constant penalty per coefficient. default reduces BIC \(p\le\sqrt n\). Supply numeric lambda use different \(\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\); separate fitter's adaptive-ridge exponent gamma. "mbic": modified BIC \(\lambda = \log(np^2/16)\). multiplicity-adjusted criterion intended sparse selection among many candidate predictors (Bogdan, Ghosh Zak-Szatkowska, 2008). constant used follows Frommlet Nuel (2016). distinct false-discovery-rate-oriented mBIC2 criterion.

text: Tom Wenseleers, Laura Lanzas & Christophe Vanderaa Tom Wenseleers tom.wenseleers@kuleuven.\ Laboratory Socioecology Social Evolution, KU Leuven \ https://bio.kuleuven./eeb/tw/research \ ORCID: 0000-0002-1434-861X

title: Fit generalized linear model with \(L_0\) or grouped row-\(L_0\) regularization subject to optional nonnegativity constraints — l0glmFit
code: # Single-channel Poisson deconvolution: shifted copies of a known PSF. single <- simul(method=2, n=500, p=500, s=.1, seed=2) fit_single <- l0glmFit(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE) l0glmMetrics(fit_single, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]  old_par <- par(no.readonly=TRUE) par(mfrow=c(1, 1), mgp=c(2, .7, 0)) # The default PSF has peak one. Scale both spike trains by the same PSF peak # to display them in signal units; negative values indicate mirroring only. spike_scale <- max(single$X) beta_single <- as.numeric(coef(fit_single)) mu_single <- as.numeric(fitted(fit_single)) height <- max(as.numeric(single$y), as.numeric(single$y_true), mu_single,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, beta_single*spike_scale) plot(single$x, single$y, type="l", col="grey65", ylim=c(-1, 1)*height*1.15,   xlab="Time", ylab="Signal / spike height (fit mirrored)",   main="Single-channel Poisson deconvolution") abline(h=0, col="grey75", lty=3) lines(single$x, single$y_true, col="grey30", lty=2) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, col="navy") lines(single$x, -mu_single, col="orange", lwd=1.5) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta, -beta_single*spike_scale, col="red") legend("topright", c("Observed signal", "True signal", "True spikes",   "Fitted signal (mirrored)", "Fitted spikes (mirrored)"),   col=c("grey65", "grey30", "navy", "orange", "red"),   lty=c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1), bty="n", cex=.75)  # Multichannel Poisson deconvolution: select rows shared across channels. # Retain every mass channel generated by the simulation. multi <- simul(method=4, n=500, p=500, s=.05, seed=2) fit_multi <- l0glmFit(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE,   parallelize=FALSE) l0glmMetrics(fit_multi, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] # The within-row scores assess channel sparsity among correctly recovered rows. dim(coef(fit_multi))                  # original predictors by response channels par(mfrow=c(2, 1)) plotMat(multi$beta_true, xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="True multichannel coefficients") plotMat(coef(fit_multi), xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="Estimated multichannel coefficients") par(old_par)  # Precluster into at most 32 channel groups, select on their summed counts, # then refine and return coefficients for every original mass channel. system.time(fit_multi_clustered <- l0glmFit(multi$X, multi$y,   family=poisson(identity), lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE,   grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=TRUE, ncores=4L,   precluster=TRUE, cluster.refit=TRUE,   control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L))) fit_multi_clustered$preclustering$clusters fit_multi_clustered$preclustering$seconds l0glmMetrics(fit_multi_clustered, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] dim(coef(fit_multi_clustered))         # all original predictors and channels  # A smooth nonnegative background: append a low-df spline basis and keep # those columns unpenalized. Poisson backgrounds add directly to the signal. B <- splines::bs(seq(0, 1, length.out=nrow(multi$X)), df=6, intercept=TRUE) alpha <- outer(c(2, 5, 3, 7, 4, 2), seq(.5, 1.5, length.out=ncol(multi$y))) set.seed(3) Y_background <- multi$y + matrix(rpois(length(multi$y), B %*% alpha),   nrow(multi$y), ncol(multi$y)) X_background <- cbind(multi$X, Matrix::Matrix(B, sparse=TRUE)) compulsory <- ncol(multi$X) + seq_len(ncol(B)) fit_background <- l0glmFit(X_background, Y_background,   family=poisson(identity), lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE,   always.include=compulsory, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE,   precluster=TRUE, ncores=4L,   control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L)) background_hat <- B %*% as.matrix(coef(fit_background)[compulsory, , drop=FALSE]) # Every original mass channel is retained in both the peak and background fit. dim(coef(fit_background)) fit_background$nuisance$seconds l0glmMetrics(fit_background,   beta_true=rbind(multi$beta_true, Matrix::Matrix(alpha, sparse=TRUE)))[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")]  # High-dimensional Gaussian regression with positive and negative effects. # Run manually: the dense design alone occupies about 4 GB. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ n <- 500L p <- 1000000L set.seed(123) X_hd <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p) support <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta_hd <- numeric(p) beta_hd[support] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) mean_hd <- as.numeric(X_hd[, support, drop=FALSE] %*% beta_hd[support]) set.seed(1) y_hd <- mean_hd + rnorm(n)  # screen="auto" activates ISIS exactly when p_eligible > 10*n. Screened fits # default to the original-p GIC preset and a relaxed refit. # Screening threads are independent of BLAS threads (nthreads). system.time(fit_hd <- l0glmFit(X_hd, y_hd, screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1)) fit_hd$screening[c("method", "screen_size", "iterations", "best_iteration", "nthreads")] fit_hd$screening$history l0glmMetrics(fit_hd, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] dim(coef(fit_hd))                    # all p rows, including screened-out zeros # Explicit alternatives: screen="SIS", "ISIS", or "none". } # }  # Basic controls: intercept constraints, dispersion and binomial fits. x <- seq(-1, 1, length.out=30) X <- matrix(x, ncol=1)  # Nonnegativity includes the Gaussian intercept. constrained <- l0glmFit(X, -2+3*x, family=gaussian(),   intercept=TRUE, nonnegative=TRUE, lambda=1e-8,   dispersion=1, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(constrained$coefficients)  # Estimate Gaussian variance from an automatic or user-supplied start. set.seed(1) y_gaussian <- 2*x + rnorm(length(x), sd=.5) automatic <- l0glmFit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=NULL, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) initialized <- l0glmFit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=-.25, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) # dispersion=.25 instead keeps the variance fixed at .25.  # A binomial intercept may remain negative with a nonnegative slope. y <- round(1000*plogis(-2+x))/1000 logistic <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=binomial(),   weights=rep(1000, length(y)), nonnegative=TRUE,   lambda=1e-8, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(logistic$coefficients)  # Gaussian validation-based stopping: keep a separate test set for assessment. set.seed(42) X_validation <- matrix(rnorm(200*40), 200, 40) y_validation <- 3 + 2*X_validation[, 1] - X_validation[, 2] + rnorm(200) train <- 1:120 fit_stopped <- l0glmFit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100,   validation=list(X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train]),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_stopped$validation$selection[c("best_iteration", "iterations", "stopped")]  # Optionally select the ISIS batch on the same validation set. # Omit nsis to keep the GIC-based default batch. fit_batch <- l0glmFit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", screen="ISIS", nsis=c(1, 3, 5, 10),   relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, validation=list(     X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train], rule="1se"),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_batch$validation[c("selected_start", "selected_nsis", "deviance")] fit_batch$validation$starts # Sparse special families: GIC preset fits, GIC tuning and three-fold CV. if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   set.seed(204)   n <- 300L   X_special <- matrix(rnorm(n*20), n, 20)   folds_special <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out=n))   family_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))    # Negative binomial: two nonzero slopes among 20 predictors.   mu_nb <- exp(.4 + .8*X_special[, 1] - .6*X_special[, 2])   y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu=mu_nb, size=2)   # nb() estimates theta; nb(theta=2) would keep it fixed at two.   nb_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_fit$theta   coef(nb_fit)   nb_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="gic", nlambda=5,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=nb_gic$lambda_best, CV=nb_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=nb_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(nb_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Three-category multinomial: only two predictor rows affect probabilities.   eta <- cbind(0, .9*X_special[, 1] - .7*X_special[, 2],     -.8*X_special[, 1] + .6*X_special[, 2])   probabilities <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))   probabilities <- probabilities/rowSums(probabilities)   y_multinomial <- factor(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)     sample.int(3, 1, prob=probabilities[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)   multinomial_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   coef(multinomial_fit)               # original-scale, zero-sum CLR rows   multinomial_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="gic", nlambda=5, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   multinomial_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="cv", nlambda=5,     nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=multinomial_gic$lambda_best, CV=multinomial_cv$lambda_best,     CV_1se=multinomial_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(multinomial_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Right-censored Cox model: two nonzero log-hazard effects, no intercept.   if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {     event_time <- rexp(n, rate=exp(.7*X_special[, 1] - .5*X_special[, 2]))     censor_time <- rexp(n, rate=.4)     y_cox <- survival::Surv(pmin(event_time, censor_time),       event_time <= censor_time)     cox_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     coef(cox_fit)     cox_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="gic", nlambda=5, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     cox_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,       relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     c(GIC=cox_gic$lambda_best, CV=cox_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=cox_cv$lambda_1se)     predict(cox_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="risk")   }   par(family_par) }

code: # Small versions of the l0glmFit deconvolution and Gaussian ISIS examples. # Five lambda values and three folds keep these examples short; increase # nlambda and nfolds for a finer search. True coefficients are only used # for plots and recovery metrics, never for fitting or choosing lambda. old_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))  # Single-channel Poisson deconvolution. # Zoom around the GIC preset; use prop_range=1 for the full lambda range. single <- simul(method=2, n=500, p=500, s=.1, seed=2) single_gic <- l0glmTune(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="gic", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, coefs.true=single$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE)  # Venetian-blind CV: train on two out of every three time points. folds <- rep(1:3, length.out=nrow(single$X)) single_cv <- l0glmTune(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="cv", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, nfolds=3, foldid=folds,   coefs.true=single$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE) c(GIC=single_gic$lambda_best, CV=single_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=single_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=single_cv$lambda_preset) single_cv$metrics[c("lambda", "cv_deviance", "cv_se")] l0glmMetrics(single_gic$fit_best, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] l0glmMetrics(single_cv$fit_best, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] # fit_1se is a full-data model, ready for prediction or coefficient extraction. fitted(single_cv$fit_1se)[1:6, , drop=FALSE]  # Grouped multichannel Poisson deconvolution, keeping every channel. multi <- simul(method=4, n=500, p=500, s=.05, seed=2) multi_gic <- l0glmTune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="gic", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, coefs.true=multi$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE)  # All channels of each time point share one fold assignment. folds <- rep(1:3, length.out=nrow(multi$X)) multi_cv <- l0glmTune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   tune="cv", nlambda=5, prop_range=.25, nfolds=3, foldid=folds,   coefs.true=multi$beta_true,   nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE, plot=TRUE) c(GIC=multi_gic$lambda_best, CV=multi_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=multi_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=multi_cv$lambda_preset) l0glmMetrics(multi_gic$fit_best, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] l0glmMetrics(multi_cv$fit_best, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] dim(coef(multi_cv$fit_1se))            # all original predictor rows and channels  # High-dimensional Gaussian regression with 60 positive/negative effects. # X alone needs about 4 GB; set p <- 20000L for a smaller example. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ n <- 500L p <- 1000000L set.seed(123) X_hd <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p) support <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta_hd <- numeric(p) beta_hd[support] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) mean_hd <- as.numeric(X_hd[, support, drop=FALSE] %*% beta_hd[support]) set.seed(1) y_hd <- mean_hd + rnorm(n)  # screen="auto" applies p_eligible > 10*n independently at each lambda, # with n equal to the training row count, including within each CV fold. hd_gic <- l0glmTune(X_hd, y_hd, family=gaussian(), tune="gic",   nlambda=5, coefs.true=beta_hd, screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1, plot=FALSE) # Screening and preprocessing are recomputed within each training fold. set.seed(42) hd_cv <- l0glmTune(X_hd, y_hd, family=gaussian(), tune="cv",   nlambda=5, nfolds=3, coefs.true=beta_hd,   screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1, plot=FALSE) c(GIC=hd_gic$lambda_best, CV=hd_cv$lambda_best,   CV_1se=hd_cv$lambda_1se, GIC_preset=hd_cv$lambda_preset) hd_cv$metrics[c("lambda", "cv_deviance", "cv_se")] l0glmMetrics(hd_gic$fit_best, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] l0glmMetrics(hd_cv$fit_best, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] hd_cv$fit_best$screening$history dim(coef(hd_cv$fit_1se))              # screened-out predictors remain zero rows } # }  # CV plots show mean held-out deviance +/- one standard error. Vertical # lines mark lambda_best, lambda_1se and the full-data GIC preset. par(old_par) # Sparse special families: GIC preset fits, GIC tuning and three-fold CV. if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   set.seed(204)   n <- 300L   X_special <- matrix(rnorm(n*20), n, 20)   folds_special <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out=n))   family_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))    # Negative binomial: two nonzero slopes among 20 predictors.   mu_nb <- exp(.4 + .8*X_special[, 1] - .6*X_special[, 2])   y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu=mu_nb, size=2)   # nb() estimates theta; nb(theta=2) would keep it fixed at two.   nb_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_fit$theta   coef(nb_fit)   nb_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="gic", nlambda=5,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=nb_gic$lambda_best, CV=nb_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=nb_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(nb_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Three-category multinomial: only two predictor rows affect probabilities.   eta <- cbind(0, .9*X_special[, 1] - .7*X_special[, 2],     -.8*X_special[, 1] + .6*X_special[, 2])   probabilities <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))   probabilities <- probabilities/rowSums(probabilities)   y_multinomial <- factor(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)     sample.int(3, 1, prob=probabilities[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)   multinomial_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   coef(multinomial_fit)               # original-scale, zero-sum CLR rows   multinomial_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="gic", nlambda=5, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   multinomial_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="cv", nlambda=5,     nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=multinomial_gic$lambda_best, CV=multinomial_cv$lambda_best,     CV_1se=multinomial_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(multinomial_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Right-censored Cox model: two nonzero log-hazard effects, no intercept.   if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {     event_time <- rexp(n, rate=exp(.7*X_special[, 1] - .5*X_special[, 2]))     censor_time <- rexp(n, rate=.4)     y_cox <- survival::Surv(pmin(event_time, censor_time),       event_time <= censor_time)     cox_fit <- l0glmFit(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     coef(cox_fit)     cox_gic <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="gic", nlambda=5, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     cox_cv <- l0glmTune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,       relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     c(GIC=cox_gic$lambda_best, CV=cox_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=cox_cv$lambda_1se)     predict(cox_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="risk")   }   par(family_par) }

B <- splines::bs(seq(0, 1, length.out=n), df=6, intercept=TRUE) set.seed(3) alpha <- outer(c(2, 5, 3, 7, 4, 2), rep(1, ncol(sim.pois.mc$y))) Y_background <- sim.pois.mc$y + matrix(rpois(length(sim.pois.mc$y), B %*% alpha),   n, ncol(sim.pois.mc$y)) compulsory <- p + seq_len(ncol(B)) fit_background <- l0nnPois(cbind(sim.pois.mc$X, Matrix::Matrix(B, sparse=TRUE)),   Y_background, always.include=compulsory, lambda="gic", ncores=4L,   precluster=TRUE, control.precluster=list(k.max=32L, rowbins=5L)) background_hat <- B %*% as.matrix(coef(fit_background)[compulsory, , drop=FALSE]) fit_background$nuisance$seconds  ## Single-channel fit uses the same nonnegative model. system.time(fit.sc <- l0nnPois(   sim.pois.mc$X,   sim.pois.mc$y[, 1L],   lambda = "gic",   grouped = FALSE,   relaxed = FALSE,   parallelize = FALSE ))  sum(fit.sc$coefficients != 0)  ## Native validation stopping with an independent repeat measurement. small <- simul(n = 300L, p = 300L, n_nonzero = 20L, m = 4L, seed = 7L) set.seed(8) y.validation <- matrix(rpois(length(small$y_true), small$y_true), 300L, 4L) validated <- l0nnPois(small$X, small$y, lambda = "gic", ncores = 2L,   validation = list(X = small$X, y = y.validation, patience = 3L)) validated$validation$deviance validated$validation$selection$history

text: lmRidge function fits ridge regression model form: $$\beta = \arg \min_{\beta} \left\{ \frac{1}{2} \| W^{1/2}(y - X \beta) \|_2^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_j \lambda_j (\beta_j - \mu_j)^2 \right\}$$   \(W\) contains observation weights, \(\lambda_j\) ridge   penalty parameters, \(\mu\) prior mean coefficients   (specified prior.mean). function supports optional bounds coefficients via   lower upper parameters can impose nonnegativity   constraints nonnegative = TRUE. scaling parameter allows scaling predictors. scaling   applied, coefficients rescaled back original scale   returned. Different solvers can specified via solver parameter: "eigen" Uses Eigen package solve ridge   regression problem using one several solvers (see method option). "bigGlm" Uses bigGlm function glmnet package solve ridge regression problem. "glmnet" alias. "osqp" Uses osqp package (Operator Splitting Quadratic Program solver) solve problem constraints. appropriate box nonnegativity constraints applied. method parameter specifies specific method used   "eigen" solver used (1=Cholesky LLT, 2=Cholesky LDLT,   3=CG incomplete Cholesky preconditioning sparse systems   diagonal preconditioning dense systems, 4=LSCG diagonal   least-squares preconditioner, 5=column-pivoted QR, 6=BDCSVD dense   systems Jacobi SVD sparse systems). LSCG uses Eigen's diagonal least-squares preconditioner without additional   external column equilibration. finite approximate LSCG solution   retained warning requested tolerance reached;   missing nonfinite solution triggers Cholesky fallback. OSQP uses   original coefficient coordinates reports warning   requested accuracy reached. failed OSQP setup solve,   infeasible/nonconvex status, invalid returned coefficient vector,   warning issued previous IRLS coefficients (clipped   bounds) retained. warning establish convergence.   Finite-tolerance solutions can change subsequent adaptive ridge   selection path. Eligible wide Eigen ridge systems use Woodbury identity solve   observation-space system dimension n, rather predictor-space   system dimension p. requested Eigen method retained.   LLT, LDLT CG, default forms Gram matrix directly dense   predictors. Sparse predictors, dense-stored working matrices   least one million entries fewer 10 percent nonzeros, use sparse   row augmentation. Set control.solver$rowaug explicitly override   automatic choice.   Dense sparse designs retain storage type; optional row augmentation   constructs sparse augmented matrix. Eigen's SVD requires dense factorization   internally even input sparse. OSQP requires sparse arrays   solver boundary.

title: Simulate sparse GLMs and deconvolution problems — simul
code: # Blurred spike trains with a known PSF, sparse peaks and an optional baseline. single <- simul("deconvolution", n=200, p=200, n_nonzero=20,   family="poisson", intercept=1, seed=2) multi <- simul("deconvolution", n=100, p=120, n_nonzero=10,   family="gaussian", m=4, intercept=c(1, 2, 3, 4), seed=2,   options=list(mean_beta=100, sd_noise=2)) dim(multi$beta_true)                  # 120 slopes plus an intercept, four channels if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   nb_spikes <- simul("deconvolution", n=100, p=100, n_nonzero=10,     family="nb", m=4, intercept=1, options=list(theta=5)) }  # Standard normal predictors, arbitrary n/p, and signed sparse coefficients. regression <- simul("normal", n=150, p=30, n_nonzero=4, intercept=1.5,   options=list(beta_range=c(-2, 2), error_sd=.5), seed=10) fit <- l0glmFit(regression$X, regression$y, family=regression$family,   intercept=regression$intercept, nonnegative=FALSE, parallelize=FALSE) l0glmMetrics(fit, beta_true=regression$beta_true)[c("gic", "F1_score", "MCC")]  # sparseGLM reads family, intercept and coefficient truth from the simulation. comparison <- sparseGLM(regression, method=c("L0glm", "lasso"), nlambda=5) l0glmMetrics(comparison)[c("method", "seconds", "gic", "F1_score", "MCC")]  # ABESS-style correlated predictors and coefficient magnitudes. abess_data <- simul("abess", n=200, p=100, n_nonzero=5,   family="binomial", intercept=-1, options=list(cortype=2, rho=.5))  # Best-subset pattern 3: decreasing effects, population SNR=2, validation data. subset_data <- simul("bestsubset", n=100, p=50, n_nonzero=5, intercept=2,   options=list(beta.type=3, rho=.5, snr=2, nval=50)) subset_data$dispersion dim(subset_data$Xval)  # Other standard links and special families use the same normal-design setup. probit_data <- simul("normal", n=100, p=20, n_nonzero=3,   family=binomial("probit"), intercept=-.5) gamma_data <- simul("normal", n=100, p=20, n_nonzero=3,   family=Gamma("log"), intercept=1, options=list(dispersion=.5)) if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {   nb_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::nb(), intercept=1, options=list(theta=3))   multinomial_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), intercept=c(.3, 0, -.3))   cox_data <- simul("normal", n=150, p=20, n_nonzero=3,     family=mgcv::cox.ph(), intercept=log(2)) # doubles the baseline hazard   cox_data$intercept                    # FALSE: no estimable Cox intercept }

title: Efficient-score screening for GLMs and special families — sisGLM
code: set.seed(1) n <- 150; p <- 300 X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p) beta <- c(1,-1,.8,-.8,rep(0,p-4)) y <- as.numeric(X%*%beta)+rnorm(n) screen <- sisGLM(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) screen$indices threaded <- sisGLM(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE,nthreads=4) identical(threaded$indices,screen$indices)  # Independent channels are screened jointly without signed cancellation. multi <- sisGLM(X,cbind(y,-y),nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) multi$indices  # Conditional screening includes the specified nuisance design. conditional <- sisGLM(X,y,nuisance=cbind(1,X[,1]),nsis=40) head(conditional$stats[conditional$ranking,])  # Offset-based outer ISIS; each candidate fit starts afresh. iterated <- sisGLM(X,y,nsis=40,iterative=TRUE,niter=10,return_stats=FALSE) iterated$history coef(iterated$fit)                 # sparse, all original predictor rows head(predict(iterated$fit,X[1:5,,drop=FALSE]))  # The same full-dimension model through the main fitting interface. fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,screen="ISIS",nsis=40,screen.maxit=10,screen.nthreads=4) fit$screening$history coef(fit) # screen="auto" (the default) enables ISIS exactly when p_eligible > 10*n. # Use screen="none" to fit the full design directly.  if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE)) {   counts <- rnbinom(n,mu=exp(.5+.4*X[,1]),size=2)   nb <- sisGLM(X,counts,family=mgcv::nb(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)   nb$theta   classes <- factor(sample(letters[1:3],n,TRUE))   multinomial <- sisGLM(X,classes,family=mgcv::multinom(2),                         nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) } if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival",quietly=TRUE)) {   time <- rexp(n,exp(.5*X[,1]))   outcome <- survival::Surv(pmin(time,2),time<=2)   cox <- sisGLM(Matrix::Matrix(X,sparse=TRUE),outcome,                 family=mgcv::cox.ph(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) }  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # One million predictors, 500 observations and 60 nonzero effects. # The dense design occupies about 4 GB; data generation is outside the timings. stopifnot(requireNamespace("SIS",quietly=TRUE)) set.seed(123) n <- 500L; p <- 1000000L; nsis <- 100L X <- matrix(rnorm(as.double(n) * p), n, p) active <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta <- numeric(p) beta[active] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) set.seed(1) y <- as.numeric(X[, active, drop = FALSE] %*% beta[active]) + rnorm(n)  # The default fit uses the GIC preset and automatic ISIS screening. t_default <- system.time(fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,family=gaussian())) l0glmMetrics(fit,beta_true=beta)[c("gic","TP","FP","FN","TN","F1_score","MCC")]  t_fast <- system.time(fast <- sisGLM(X, y, nsis = nsis)) t_one <- system.time(one <- sisGLM(X, y, nsis = nsis, nthreads = 1L)) # Screening only: this helper runs the initial screen in SIS 1.5 without its # subsequent LASSO fit. Its internal interface may vary between SIS versions. sis_screen <- getFromNamespace("obtain.ix0","SIS") t_screen <- system.time(reference <- sis_screen(X,y,s1=NULL,s2=NULL,   family="gaussian",nsis=nsis,iter=FALSE,varISIS="vanilla",perm=FALSE,   q=1,greedy=FALSE,greedy.size=1L,iterind=0L))  data.frame(method=c("sisGLM, default threads","sisGLM, one thread","SIS screen"),   seconds=c(t_fast[["elapsed"]],t_one[["elapsed"]],t_screen[["elapsed"]]))  # Compare the initial screening rank, including all one million predictors. identical(fast$indices,as.integer(reference$ix0))       # TRUE identical(fast$ranking,as.integer(reference$ix0all))    # TRUE identical(one$ranking,fast$ranking)                   # TRUE  # Complete models: both timings include screening and variable selection. t_SIS <- system.time(sis_fit <- SIS::SIS(X,y,family="gaussian",nsis=nsis,   iter=FALSE,penalty="lasso",tune="bic",standardize=FALSE,parallel=FALSE,seed=123L)) t_L0glm <- system.time(l0_fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,   screen="SIS",nsis=nsis,lambda="gic",relaxed=TRUE)) data.frame(method=c("SIS + BIC LASSO","SIS + L0glm GIC preset"),   seconds=c(t_SIS[["elapsed"]],t_L0glm[["elapsed"]])) l0glmMetrics(l0_fit,beta_true=beta)[c("gic","TP","FP","F1_score","MCC")]  # Shared screening also makes end-to-end comparisons convenient for other # methods. Change screen to "ISIS" for method-specific iterative screening. comparison <- sparseGLM(X,y,method=c("L0glm","lasso","relaxed_lasso"),   screen="SIS",nsis=nsis,tune="bic",nlambda=10,beta_true=beta,intercept=FALSE,   lambda=list(L0glm=presetLambda("gic",p,n)),options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE))) l0glmMetrics(comparison)[c("method","screen","seconds","bic","TP","FP","F1_score","MCC")] } # }

code: # Sparse Gaussian regression. set.seed(1) X <- matrix(rnorm(360),60,6) truth <- c(2,-1,rep(0,4)) y <- as.numeric(X %*% truth + rnorm(60)) comparison <- sparseGLM(X,y,method=c("lasso","relaxed_lasso"),   tune="gic",nlambda=5,beta_true=truth) l0glmMetrics(comparison)[c("method","seconds","gic","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")] plot(comparison,which=c(1,2))  # The same SIS/ISIS controls apply to every supported method. Each ISIS round # uses that method's own selected model to screen for additional predictors. set.seed(2) wide <- matrix(rnorm(100*2000),100,2000) truth_wide <- c(3,-2,1.5,rep(0,1997)) y_wide <- as.numeric(wide%*%truth_wide)+rnorm(100) screened <- sparseGLM(wide,y_wide,method=c("L0glm","lasso","relaxed_lasso"),   screen="ISIS",nsis=10,nlambda=5,beta_true=truth_wide,   lambda=list(L0glm=presetLambda("gic",ncol(wide),nrow(wide))),   options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE))) l0glmMetrics(screened)[c("method","screen","seconds","gic","TP","FP","F1_score","MCC")] # With tune="cv", all screening and adaptive pilots use training rows only. screened_cv <- sparseGLM(wide,y_wide,method="lasso",screen="SIS",nsis=20,   tune="cv",nfolds=3,nlambda=5,beta_true=truth_wide) l0glmMetrics(screened_cv)[c("method","screen","seconds","TP","FP","F1_score","MCC")]  # Blurred Poisson spike trains: smaller versions of the single/multichannel # deconvolution benchmarks. MCP and SCAD are omitted because they were slow # on the large deconvolution examples. All times below are measured locally. comparison_methods <- c("L0glm","abess","L0Learn","lasso","relaxed_lasso",                         "adaptive_lasso","adaptive_relaxed_lasso") fields <- c("method","seconds","gic","deviance","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")  # Single channel: 50 spikes among 500 candidate locations. single <- simul(method=2,n=500,p=500,s=.1,seed=2) lambda_gic <- log(ncol(single$X))*log(log(nrow(single$X))) comparison_single <- sparseGLM(single,family=poisson(identity),   method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,   nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls",   support.size=1:100,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),   options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=FALSE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE))) l0glmMetrics(comparison_single)[fields] plot(comparison_single,which=c(1,2,4,5))  # Multichannel: use 100 time points and six abundant mass channels for speed. multi <- simul(method=4,n=100,p=100,s=.1,seed=2) keep <- head(order(Matrix::colSums(multi$y),decreasing=TRUE),6) for (name in c("y","y_true","beta_true")) multi[[name]] <- multi[[name]][,keep,drop=FALSE] lambda_gic <- log(ncol(multi$X))*log(log(nrow(multi$X))) comparison_multi <- sparseGLM(multi,family=poisson(identity),   method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,   nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls_grouped",   support.size=1:20,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),   options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE))) # ABESS and glmnet select rows jointly using Gaussian shared-row-weight WLS; # L0glm fits the exact grouped Poisson model. L0Learn fits channels independently. # GIC, deviance and prediction R-squared always use the original Poisson model. l0glmMetrics(comparison_multi)[c(fields,"within_row_F1_score","within_row_MCC")]  plot(comparison_multi,which=c(1,4),type="coefs",channels="all") plot(comparison_multi,which=c(1,2,4,5),channels="mean") # One ground-truth/estimate pair; heatmaps default to which=1. plot(comparison_multi,type="heatmap") # Two pages, each with its own ground-truth/estimate pair. plot(comparison_multi,type="heatmap",which=c(1,2))
